paper.title: Online Learning via Offline Greedy Algorithms: Applications in Market Design and Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Full-information adversarial online learning version of problem (1) (offline problem with extended robust, Blackwell reducible greedy algorithm)
unmapped: gamma-approximate regret benchmark (gamma * best fixed point in hindsight)
nonlinear reward functions f_t: D -> [0,1] from a function class F closed under addition
offline problem admits an extended (gamma,delta)-robust, Blackwell-reducible iterative greedy algorithm
settings.definition_quote: In each round $t\in [T]$,  $\adv$ picks a function $f_t\in\funcspace$ and simultaneously $\alg$ takes an action by picking a feasible point $\zbf_t\in \constraint$. ... (i)~full information feedback, where $\alg$ observes the entire function $f_t$ after choosing $\zbf_t$

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit-information adversarial online learning version of problem (1)
unmapped: nonlinear reward functions from class F
offline problem admits an extended (gamma,delta)-robust, bandit-Blackwell-reducible iterative greedy algorithm
settings.definition_quote: (ii)~bandit feedback, where $\alg$ only observes the quantity $f_t(\zbf_t)$ after choosing $\zbf_t$.

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Vector-payoff Blackwell approachability game; guarantee is distance of average payoff to a target set, not bandit regret.
unmapped: biaffine vector payoff, target set S response-satisfiable, l_infinity distance
settings.definition_quote: A Blackwell sequential game is a repeated two-player game characterized by a tuple $\blackwellsequentialgame$.

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Vector-payoff approachability game with costly exploration; objective is distance to target set plus exploration penalty.
unmapped: player receives unbiased payoff estimate only when exploring, paying cost D(p) per exploration
settings.definition_quote: In this variant, player 1 makes an additional decision in each round: whether to \emph{explore} or not. Only if player 1 chooses to explore in round $t$, do they receive the unbiased estimator $\hat{\pbf}(\bm{x}_t, \bm{y}_t)$ ... player 1 is punished by an additive cost $D(\pbf)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Online sequential submodular maximization / product ranking (full information)
unmapped: actions are rankings of n items
settings.definition_quote: We study the online user-engagement-maximization ranking problem where on every round $t,$ a distribution over patience level $\bm{\lambda}_t$ and the expected probability of click function $f_t$ ... are chosen adversarially. ... After choosing the ranking, the platform observes the function $f_t$ in the full-information setting.

settings.name_in_paper: Online sequential submodular maximization / product ranking (bandit)
unmapped: actions are rankings of n items
settings.definition_quote: In the bandit setting, the platform \emph{only} observes whether or not the consumer clicks on at least one item, but not which item was clicked on.

settings.name_in_paper: Maximizing multiple reserves (MMR), online full information
unmapped: actions are personalized reserve vectors in R^n (finite grid of m reserve values) for a second-price auction
settings.definition_quote: each round $t \in [T]$ involves the seller choosing a set of reserves $\rbf_t$ and the adversary choosing a valuation profile $\vibf_t$. In the online full information setting, the seller observes the valuation profile and gets credit for the resulting revenue.
In the online bandit setting, the seller observes just the resulting revenue and does not observe the bidders' valuations or even the identity of the winner.

settings.name_in_paper: Online discretized non-monotone submodular maximization (full information)
unmapped: domain R^n with |R| = m grid values per coordinate
settings.definition_quote: we essentially consider discrete functions $f:\coordinatevalues^n\rightarrow[0,1]$ that satisfy a discrete version of (weak-DR) submodularity ... our goal in the offline problem is to solve the optimization problem $\max_{\zbf\in \coordinatevalues^n} f(\zbf)$.

unmapped: domain R^n with |R| = m grid values per coordinate
settings.definition_quote: in the online bandit setting, there exists an online learning algorithm that obtains ... $\tfrac12$-regret.

settings.name_in_paper: Online L-Lipschitz non-monotone continuous submodular maximization on [0,1]^n (full information)
unmapped: non-monotone weak-DR continuous submodular rewards on hypercube [0,1]^n
settings.definition_quote: for the problem of maximizing a coordinate-wise $L$-Lipschitz non-monotone (continuous) submodular function in the online full-information setting

settings.name_in_paper: Online L-Lipschitz non-monotone continuous submodular maximization on [0,1]^n (bandit)
unmapped: non-monotone weak-DR continuous submodular rewards on hypercube
settings.definition_quote: Furthermore, in the online bandit setting, there exists a learning algorithm that obtains $\bigO{n L^{2/5}T^{4/5}\log^{1/3} (LT)}$ $\tfrac12$-regret

settings.name_in_paper: Online strong-DR monotone submodular maximization over downward closed convex polytope (full information)
unmapped: rewards are monotone strong-DR submodular (non-concave) functions
gradient l_inf norm bounded by U
settings.definition_quote: In the online problem, we consider an adversarial sequence of strong-DR submodular functions $f_1,\ldots,f_T$, where for each $1\leq t\leq T$, $f_t:\mathcal{P}\rightarrow[0,1]$ for some downward closed polynomial-time separable convex polytope ... $f_t$ is $L$-Lipschitz smooth and $||\nabla f_t(\zbf)||_\infty\leq U$

algorithms.name: Online-IG (full-information online learning meta-algorithm, N parallel Blackwell algorithms)
Bandit-IG (bandit online learning meta-algorithm using N bandit Blackwell algorithms)
AlgBB (Bandit Blackwell online algorithm, explore w.p. q)

Full-information online Frank-Wolfe with Blackwell algorithms (Algorithm online-DR-SM)

symbols.D_p: l_infinity diameter of the payoff function p
symbols.d_payoff: dimension of the Blackwell game / vector payoff

source.label: def:blackwell-thm
source.quote: A  closed and convex target set $S$ is $O(\diameter{\pbf}\log(d)^{1/2}T^{-1/2})$-approachable in the Blackwell sequential game $\blackwellsequentialgame$ if and only if the set $S$ is response-satisfiable

results.notes: Approachability bound (l_inf distance of average payoff to S), not regret; adaptation of Blackwell (1956). Deterministic guarantee; 'expectation' chosen nominally.

symbols.D_p: l_infinity diameter of payoff p (also the exploration cost)
symbols.D_phat: l_infinity diameter of the unbiased payoff estimator p-hat

source.label: thm:bandit-blackwell-thm
source.quote: A closed convex set $S$ is $\bigO{{D(\pbf)}^{1/3}\diameter{\hat{\pbf}}^{2/3}(\log d)^{1/3}T^{-1/3}}$-bandit-approachable in the bandit Blackwell sequential game ... if and only if $S$ is response-satisfiable

results.notes: Bound on l_inf distance plus time-averaged exploration penalty.

symbols.D_low: min{D(p), D(p)} as defined in the paper (equals D(p))

conditions: hard instance: X = simplex over n actions, Y={0,1}^n, p(x,y)=x^T y 1 - y, S non-positive orthant

source.label: thm:bandit-blackwell-lower-bound
source.quote: In a bandit Blackwell sequential game, $\banditblackwellsequentialgame,$  there exists an adversary's strategy such that for every player 1's strategy, the resulting sequence of actions satisfy: ... $\ge \bigOmega{\Dbottom T^{-1/3}}$

results.notes: Lower bound on distance-to-set plus exploration penalty; D_low as printed is min{D(p),D(p)}.

symbols.N_sub: number of subproblems of the offline greedy algorithm
symbols.delta_rob: robustness parameter delta of extended (gamma,delta)-robust approximation

source.label: thm:full-info-online-meta
source.quote: Then, for this online problem, $\onlinemeta$ runs in polynomial time and  satisfies the following $\gamma$-regret bound: $\gamma\textrm{-regret}\left(\onlinemeta \right)\leq O\left(\diameter{\pbf} N\delta\sqrt{\log(\payoffdimension)T}\right)$

results.notes: gamma-regret. Example gives O(k sqrt(T log n)) (1-1/e)-regret for monotone SM with cardinality k.

symbols.D_phat: l_infinity diameter of unbiased payoff estimator

conditions: offline algorithm is bandit Blackwell reducible
tuning: exploration probability q tuned with T as in Theorem bandit-blackwell-thm

source.label: thm:banditILO
source.quote: Then, for this online problem, $\banditmeta$  runs in polynomial time and  satisfies the following $\gamma$-regret bound: \gamma\textrm{-regret}\left(\banditmeta \right)\leq \bigO{{D(\pbf)}^{1/3}{D(\hat{\pbf})}^{2/3}N\delta\left(\log(\payoffdimension)\right)^{1/3} T^{2/3}}

results.notes: gamma-regret. Example gives O(k n^{2/3} (log n)^{1/3} T^{2/3}) (1-1/e)-regret for monotone SM with cardinality.

source.label: thm:seqsub
source.quote: For the problem of maximizing sequential submodular functions in the online full information setting, there exists a learning algorithm that obtains $\bigO{n\sqrt{T\log{n}}}$ $\frac12$-regret

results.notes: 1/2-regret. Corollary cor:rank-general (product ranking) restates the same bound.

source.label: thm:seqsub
source.quote: Furthermore, in the online bandit setting, there exists a learning algorithm that obtains $\bigO{n^{5/3}\left(\log{n}\right)^{1/3}T^{2/3}}$ $\tfrac12$-regret

conditions: benchmark over reserves in the finite grid R^n

source.label: thm:mmr
source.quote: for the problem of maximizing personalized reserve prices in the online full information setting, there exists a learning algorithm that obtains $\bigO{n T^{1/2} \log^{1/2} m}$ $\tfrac12$-regret

conditions: benchmark over reserves in the finite grid R^n

source.label: thm:mmr
source.quote: Furthermore, in the online bandit setting, there exists a learning algorithm that obtains $\bigO{n m^{2/3} T^{2/3} \log^{1/3} m}$ $\tfrac12$-regret

tuning: discretization of reserves chosen depending on T

source.label: cor:mmr
source.quote: there exists a learning algorithm that obtains $\bigO{n T^{1/2} \log^{1/2} T}$ $\tfrac12$-regret ... the benchmark in the regret bounds is $\frac{1}{2}\max_{\rbf\in [0,1]^n}\sum_{t=1}^T f(\rbf, \vibf_t)$.

tuning: discretization of reserves chosen depending on T

source.label: cor:mmr
source.quote: Furthermore, in the online bandit setting, there exists a learning algorithm that obtains $\bigO{n^{3/5}T^{4/5}\log^{1/3}(nT)}$ $\tfrac12$-regret.

source.label: thm:DR-SM
source.quote: Then, under full-information setting, \Cref{alg:online-DR-SM} with $N$ iterations obtains $\bigO{{\diampolytope}U\sqrt{Tn\log{n}} + \frac{TL{\diampolytope}^2}{N}}$ $\gamma_N$-regret

symbols.U_grad: bound on l_inf norm of gradients

tuning: N = sqrt(T) L R_P / (U sqrt(n log n))

source.label: thm:DR-SM
source.quote: By setting $N= \frac{\sqrt{T}LR_{\mathcal{P}}}{U\sqrt{n\log{n}}}$, we get $\bigO{{\diampolytope}U\sqrt{Tn\log{n}}}$ $\gamma_N$-regret.

symbols.U_grad: bound on l_inf norm of gradients

conditions: polytope is the matroid polytope of a matroid with |V|=n and rank R
tuning: N = sqrt(T) L R / (U n sqrt(n log n))

source.label: corr:strong-DR-SM-matroid
source.quote: When we restrict our domain to $\Pcal_{M}$ ... we obtain a total regret of $\bigO{RU\sqrt{Tn\log{n}} + \frac{TL{R}^2}{Nn}}$ for \Cref{alg:online-DR-SM}. Setting $N= \frac{\sqrt{T}LR}{Un\sqrt{n\log{n}}}$, we get $\bigO{RU\sqrt{Tn\log{n}}}$ $\gamma_N$-regret.

results.notes: Untuned version O(R U sqrt(Tn log n) + T L R^2/(N n)) also stated.
